observation.visible_scene: A close-up kitchen scene: a person in a white top and cream trousers stands behind a white counter on which sits a black induction cooktop holding a dark frying pan with several glossy red-brown sausages; thin steam/smoke wisps rise from the pan. The person's right hand (upper right) grips a wooden slotted spatula whose head rests in the pan over the sausages; a clear glass plate is partly visible at the right edge. The person's left arm, wearing a white beaded bracelet, is at the left; its reflection appears as a second bracelet-like curve on the glossy cooktop surface (a reflection, not a separate object). White cabinet fronts with a horizontal handle form the blurred background.
visible_changes: Camera framing gradually widens/pulls back: at t=0 the pan's lower rim is cut off by the bottom edge and only 2-3 sausages are partly visible; by t=3.2 the whole pan, its handle, and three roughly parallel sausages are fully in frame.
Left arm/hand: at t=0-0.08 it is motion-blurred near the top-left, then from t=0.16 onward it settles resting on the counter edge and stays there.

Spatula and sausages: the right hand keeps holding the spatula throughout; the spatula head tilts more upright and lifts slightly above the pan around t=1.6-2.2, then presses back down onto the middle sausage from t=2.3 to the end, nudging/turning the sausages so their layout shifts from overlapping to three side-by-side links.
Steam continues to rise from the pan across the whole excerpt.
outside_clip_unknowns: Why the sausages were placed in the pan and the intended cooking outcome (the excerpt ends mid-process).
What the left hand was doing before the motion-blurred frame at t=0.
uncertain_details: Whether the spatula fully flips a sausage or only shifts/rolls it is not clearly resolved due to blur and the pan's edge.
The exact camera motion (zoom-out vs. physical pull-back) is inferred only from the growing field of view; background scale change is subtle.
The number of sausages at the very start is hard to fix because of occlusion by the spatula head and the cropped frame.
